translation.english_title: We need a heart that can bear anything

english_lines: We need a heart that can bear anything,
In this world, enmity and blame strike like snakes —
We need a heart that can bear anything,
notes: The repeated title line is kept repeated rather than reduced to a single refrain reference.
`பகையும் பழியும் பாம்பெனத் தீண்டும்` retains the snake image and the direct prison/torture sequence remains unsoftened.
The abbreviated source refrain cue is preserved rather than expanded.

english_lines: Look at the life of Socrates,
Look also at the end of deathless Gandhi,
Do not fall because of pain,
Do not wither under trial — you, do not wither,
Do not wither under trial — what comes...
notes: `சாகாத காந்தி` remains `deathless Gandhi`, preserving Kalaignar's paradoxical memorial phrase.
The repeated `வாடாதே` is retained as repeated exhortation rather than stylistically varied.

english_lines: Life called honey itself will turn into a scorpion,
In public life, death at the battlefront is joy,
Arrogance may roar, the army may pounce,
Seeing fury, do not scatter — let the heart not scatter,
Hearing slander, do not wilt — enmity...
notes: The honey-to-scorpion reversal is retained literally; it is one of the stanza's central rhetorical blows.
`போர்முனைச் சாவே பொதுவாழ்வில் இன்பம்` remains the stark `death at the battlefront is joy in public life`; it is not softened into sacrifice/service language.
`ஆணவம் / ராணுவம்` is translated semantically as arrogance / army without inventing an English rhyme at the cost of meaning.

translator_notes: The translation preserves the song as political-philosophical exhortation: snake, prison, torture, Socrates, deathless Gandhi, honey/scorpion, battlefront death, arrogance, army, fury and slander all remain explicit.
The source's repetitions are kept as rhetorical insistence rather than polished away.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
